aAbout: World Monitor is a free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) intelligence dashboard by Elie Habib, hosted at worldmonitor.app and also self-hostable from its public source. Its homepage, dated 26 October 2026, cites 468 news and OSINT feeds and 59 map layer types spanning geopolitics, conflicts, military movements, fires, earthquakes, aircraft, ships, markets and infrastructure, correlated so converging events surface together. The same codebase powers six variants — geopolitics, tech, finance, commodity, energy and positive news — plus native desktop apps, a REST API and an MCP server. No webcam feature appears on its official pages.
aStrengths: World Monitor is the broader and more open instrument: dozens of fused layer types — conflicts, chokepoints, fires, quakes, aircraft, ships, markets, cables and datacentres — on one map, in six specialised variants, with a 3D globe, desktop apps, a documented REST API and MCP server, and AGPL-3.0 source you can inspect or self-host. It is genuinely free at the core, with no signup wall, and its layer and feed counts are published on a dated homepage rather than left vague.
bAbout: LiveUAMap — the Live Universal Awareness Map — is an independent news and information site founded in 2014 to cover the Ukrainian conflict, expanding by viewer request to more than 30 regions and topics including Syria and Israel-Palestine. Its map-centric model uses proprietary AI web crawlers to find newsworthy stories, which are forwarded to a group of expert analysts for fact-checking before editors decide what appears on the map. It keeps a complete chronological archive for researching past events, runs on the web and in iOS and Android apps, and is funded mainly by advertising.
bStrengths: LiveUAMap is the more trustworthy newsroom: more than a decade of continuous operation since 2014, a defined editorial method — crawlers surface, analysts fact-check, editors decide — and a chronological archive that lets you research how an event unfolded, not just where it is now. Its per-region focus, iOS and Android apps with breaking-news and security notifications, satellite maps on PRO, and custom regions make it a working daily briefing tool, and its paid tiers are the cheapest here by a wide margin.
betterAnswer: They solve different problems. World Monitor is a free, open-source multi-layer dashboard that fuses news, conflicts, hazards, transport and markets so you can spot converging signals yourself. LiveUAMap is a veteran editorial news map that trades breadth for verification — fewer data types, but a human-checked, archived record across 30+ regions. If you want signals, open World Monitor; if you want checked stories, open LiveUAMap.

verdictA: Choose World Monitor if you want the widest live picture — many signal types fused on one free map, with developer access and open source — and you are comfortable weighing fused feeds and AI briefs yourself.
verdictB: Choose LiveUAMap if you follow specific conflicts or regions and want each plotted story to have passed human fact-checking first, with an archive, mobile apps and a very cheap ad-free or PRO tier.
verdictLine: World Monitor is the breadth play — a free, open-source dashboard that fuses everything it can ingest. LiveUAMap is the trust play — a slower, narrower news map where people verify stories before they are plotted. Neither shows you live cameras; both show you live events, by opposite methods.
worldEye: If what you actually want from either map is to see a place, not just read about it, WorldEye is the third shape: a hosted 3D globe that opens free in any browser with no signup — 74,229 public cameras across 105 countries, alongside live flights, ships, satellites, weather, earthquakes and wildfires in the same view. It does not fuse World Monitor's breadth of intel feeds or match LiveUAMap's analyst-verified newsroom and archive, and its Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) buys an OSINT toolkit and intel feeds rather than either of those.
